fingerprints.a: The degree of financial leverage is:
fingerprints.b: The degree of financial leverage (DFL) formula when preferred stock exists is:

response_a.overall_rationale: Correctness holds. The after-tax form of the leverage formula is algebraically identical to the standard one, and substituting the four given figures yields 225,000 over 174,000, which rounds to the listed 1.29. Coverage is complete, since a multiple-choice item asks for one value, and the closing line names it. Focus is precise, with no sentence that fails to advance the calculation, and Tone suits a homework question. Clarity is what costs the response its overall rating. The after-tax variant is not the form most textbooks print, and the response never states that the two are equivalent. A reader checking against their own notes therefore has to derive the equivalence before trusting a correct result. The whole derivation is also compressed into a single display, moving from the bracketed expression straight to 174,000 without showing the subtraction that produced it. Neither gap changes the answer, but both leave the reader reconstructing work the response could have shown.

focus_checkboxes: Contains unnecessary repetition or redundant phrasing
response_b.overall_rationale: Clarity is the strength here. The standard leverage formula for a firm carrying preferred stock appears first, and the four inputs are listed under it. Each stage of the arithmetic then occupies its own display, so the gross-up of the preferred dividend to a pre-tax 10,000 and the denominator of 290,000 can both be checked at a glance. That separation matters on this item, because one of the five options is the figure a reader lands on by handling the tax adjustment the wrong way round. Correctness is sound throughout, and the final division of 375,000 by 290,000 rounds to the listed 1.29. Coverage is complete, and Tone fits a homework question. Focus is the single deduction, and it is mild. The block of inputs repeats four figures the question had already supplied, and three separate displays would have served as two. The overall rating stays at the top because the axes that decide a calculation question, Correctness and Clarity, are both unblemished.

preference_explanation: Clarity decided this, and Focus is the axis that runs the other way. Both responses reach 1.29, and both are arithmetically sound. Neither Correctness nor Coverage separates them. On Clarity, @Response_B uses the leverage formula in the form textbooks print, gives the preferred dividend gross-up its own labelled step, and puts the pre-tax 10,000 and the denominator 290,000 on lines of their own. A reader can check each stage against their own notes without reconstructing anything. @Response_A compresses the whole derivation into one chained display and uses the after-tax variant of the formula without saying that the two forms are equivalent, so the same reader has to verify the route before trusting the result. On Focus, @Response_A is the stronger of the two, carrying nothing that fails to advance the calculation, while @Response_B repeats the four given figures in a list of inputs. That advantage is smaller than the Clarity gap, because a repeated figure costs a reader seconds, while an unexplained formula costs them the check itself. The margin is moderate rather than large, since @Response_A is correct, complete and lands on the same option.
